design: MicroDuck battery backpack V2 rev M (minimal: bigger battery, today's switch and DFR1202 moved in), printable frame and cap (build_v2.py). Every built feature and hole is listed with its reason; checks.py fails on a built feature missing here, an entry not built, an empty field or an unknown premise.

P-BAT.says: 2S 3000 mAh pack, envelope 74 x 34 x 20 mm (largest published size: listing text 72 x 34 x 20, listing drawing 74 x 34 x 19), leads out of the middle of one end face
P-BAT.source: Amazon B08LZ8L4YD listing text and drawing; ../battery-v2-concept-20261119/README.md

P-DFR.says: DFRobot DFR1202 5 V buck, 30 x 26 x 8 mm
P-DFR.source: DFRobot DFR1202 wiki; concept README F5

P-POSTS.says: the backpack fixes to the OpenRB pack posts with four M2 x 6 at (y, z) (+-16.1, 26) and (+-16.1, -36.5), front face x -45

P-SHELL.says: the shell rear lips reach behind x -45 (to x -46.39): side lips |y| 20-29.7 z 7-31, top lip z 31-36 |y| < 28

P-SEAT.says: the seated robot (Brain sit) must keep 10 mm or more under the backpack: lowest point z -46.0
P-SEAT.source: Shawn 2026-11-20 '会影响坐下吗'; concept rev B

P-ENV.says: no growth above z 43 or wider than |y| 32.05; behind x -75.55 only the switch rocker and flange (8.0 mm, z 28.7..42.5), clear of the flight harness
P-ENV.source: DESIGN-CONTRACT.json; concept README F1; rev 1 had no part behind x -75.55 (the PV6 bezel stood 1.5 behind)

P-LEGS.says: the legs swing beside the lower tier; leg clearance at least the approved concept B's 7.6 mm (hip pitch +-30, roll +-10)

P-FIT.says: every printed fit takes its numbers from cad-practice/print_fit.py (H2S: M2 clear vertical 2.5, pilot 1.95, locating 0.15/side, loose horizontal 0.5/side, 0.4 bed chamfer)

P-INSERT.says: with the frame screwed on the robot, the boards, the battery with its foam, the diode and the pads go in from the open back along the guide's paths, then the cap with the button; no fixed feature may stand in those paths
P-INSERT.source: guide print gate steps_audit bv2-battery failure on rev B1 (commit e33bd450) and the coordinator's fix brief 2026-11-20; checked by the insertion sweep in checks.py

P-ACCESS.says: each screw has a 4 mm driver corridor over 60 mm and no screw hole runs parallel and close to a wall

P-SCREWS.says: only even M2 lengths 4/6/8/10 are in stock

P-ROBUST.says: no snaps, flexures, hooks or latches and nothing under 1.2 mm on a part that rides on the robot; boards are held by foam tape and ribs

P-FLIGHT.says: the flight pack sits on the backpack 6.9 mm back on its wing plate; nothing may touch its harness or plates; its wing plate has cheeks 1.55 mm behind its back face at |y| 18.9-32.1, z -1 to 42.5

P-PLUGS.says: plug 3 (XT30) and plug 4 (MR30) leads leave the backpack to the robot through the left wing's step floor

P-PRINT.says: both parts print in Orange on the X1C, Elegoo or H2S without supports

P-MIN.says: minimal change: only the battery is new; the robot's own Swann 39 switch (with its switch lead, plug 1 and plug 2), DFR1202 and swap leads move in; nothing else is bought; charging is switch off and the battery's 3-pin balance plug into the B3 without opening the pack
P-MIN.source: Shawn 2026-11-20: "就是把电池换大 然后重做背包 充电用电池的3针头直接插在充电器上充 这样也不用拆包 最小改造"; "重做背包"

P-SWITCH.says: Swann 39 rocker (RoboClub, on the robot): flange 30 x 13.8 x 1.5, rocker 25 x 10, 6.5 tall beyond the flange (8.0 proud of the panel face), body 27.3 x 11.5 about 16 deep, lugs to 25.5 behind the panel face; cutout 27.5 x 12.3 in a 3 mm panel; snap wings reach y +-16.22
P-SWITCH.source: microduck_rl/cmu/hardware/battery-backpack/DESIGN-D010.md, envelopes/switch_swann-world.stl and build.json (Shawn measured the body 11.5, 2026-10-17)

P-HARNESS.says: the flight pack's cross harness lies behind the backpack at z 4..28, |y| < 33, reaching 7.75 mm behind the cap in flight
P-HARNESS.source: extensions/flight-20261110/cad/build/dummy_cross_harness-world.stl (x -90.2..-50.4, z 4..28) with the 6.9 mm flight offset

P-XH.says: the battery's balance plug is a JST XH-3P housing, 9.9 x 5.75 x 7.8 mm, on the pack's balance lead out of its top face; the HTRC B3 Pro Compact charges a 2S pack through its 3-pin port
P-XH.source: JST XH drawing (XHP-3); CURRENT-STATE parts_battery_charging (B3 in hand, 3-pin port); listing B08LZ8L4YD (XH-3P)

frame.what: lower tier x -75.55..-45, y -25.3..21.8, z -46..-15.2 under today's upper tier, floor 1.4
problems: the 74 mm pack does not fit today's 77 mm-tall box with lead room
frame.purpose: holds the upright pack's lower part while the seated robot keeps 10 mm under it
frame.simpler: pack lying lengthwise (concept D) adds 48.5 mm depth; growing upward breaks z 43; floor 1.4 (rev B 2.1 held a 0.81 pad pocket, gone)
frame.validation: contract z_min > -46.05; legsit.py seated and leg clearances
frame.change_when: a shorter pack is chosen or the sit pose changes

frame.what: 3.8 mm chamfer on the lower tier's front-right vertical edge (2.5 inside)
problems: the right leg's swing passes the lower tier's front-right corner
frame.purpose: leg clearance without narrowing the pack column
frame.simpler: a narrower lower tier would cut into the pack column

frame.what: 1.8 mm chamfer on the lower tier's front-left vertical edge (x -45, y 21.8)
problems: the left leg (hip pitch +30, roll -10) passed the square front-left bottom corner at 7.41 mm after the lower tier was widened 1.8 mm for the driver corridor, under the approved concept's 7.6
frame.purpose: restore the left leg clearance without giving back the driver corridor
frame.simpler: narrowing the lower tier again closes the lower-left fixing screw's 4 mm corridor
frame.validation: legsit.py leg clearance; wall check (1.34 mm at the inner corner)
frame.change_when: the lower tier width or the leg sweep changes

frame.what: today's upper tier outline x -75.55..-45, |y| 32.05, z -15.2..43, walls 1.7, roof 1.4, front wall 2.0
problems: the backpack must keep today's footprint on the robot
frame.purpose: the shell that carries the DFR1202, the switch body and the pack's upper part
frame.simpler: it is today's printed outline; the roof is 1.4 (rev B 1.7) to give the switch body its 11.5 mm
frame.validation: contract bounds; flight-pack overlap 0; wall check >= 1.2
frame.change_when: the robot's back or the flight pack changes

frame.what: 11.9 mm free height between the pack top (z 29.4 + 0.3 play) and the roof (z 41.6), over the whole column
problems: the pack leads (XT30, DC5.5, balance) exit the middle of its top face
the switch body (11.5) lies over the pack's left part
plug 1 and the parked balance plug sit on the right
frame.purpose: room for the switch body, plug 1, the balance plug and the bent leads without pressing the pack
frame.simpler: a lower roof would crush the switch and leads; a higher roof breaks z 43
frame.validation: switch, plug 1 and balance plug envelope overlap 0 (checks.py); top stops clear of the lead exit
frame.change_when: the pack or its lead exit changes

frame.what: inner wall y -25.3..-23.6, x -70.3..-47, from the step floor to z 17
problems: the pack must not shift right into the right wing
frame.purpose: right side of the battery column in the upper tier
frame.simpler: kept from rev B as printed in the concept; full height costs material and blocks fingers placing plug 1

frame.what: 1.5 mm rib y 11.0..12.5: floor stub to z -41.5 and upper part z -32..17
problems: the pack must not shift left into the DFR1202 wing
frame.purpose: left side of the battery column, split around the lower-left fixing screw's driver corridor
frame.simpler: a full rib blocks the lower-left driver corridor
frame.validation: access_check on fix y+16.1 z-36.5; battery overlap 0

frame.what: rib thickened to y 13.2 over the DFR1202's height
problems: the DFR1202 needs a flat face to take its foam tape
frame.purpose: tape face for the DFR1202 at y 13.2
frame.simpler: taping to the 1.5 rib alone leaves the board loose in y

frame.what: floor block x -49.3..-47, y -12..8, z to -41
problems: the pack must not slide forward onto the fixing screw heads
frame.purpose: front stop at the pack's bottom
frame.simpler: the front wall alone lets the pack hit the screw heads

frame.what: two pillars x -52.3..-49.3, y -14..-10 and -4..0, from the pack top + play to the roof
problems: the pack must not lift on a fall
frame.purpose: front top stops clear of the lead exit and of the switch lugs (y 2.3..14.5 at x -59..-50)
frame.simpler: full-width ribs (concept) block the leads when the pack slides in
frame.validation: battery and switch overlap 0; lead exit open

problems: the DFR1202 must not slide down on its tape

frame.what: two high cap screw bosses dia 5, 5 mm long: left (29, 19) and right (-29, 39)
problems: the cap must be held without snaps
frame.purpose: screw bosses for the cap's two upper M2 x 8
frame.simpler: snaps or a slide-on cap are banned; tape cannot be reopened
frame.validation: fit_check engagement; access_check; insertion sweep (outside every part's path)

frame.what: two full-depth columns from the front wall to the back face carrying the low cap screws: lower-left wing y 15.1..20.15, z -30.5..-25.5 (screw at 17.6, -28) joined to the side wall; right wing y -30.4..-25.25, z -13.55..-4.5 (screw at -27.825, -8) from wall to column wall on the step floor
problems: the cap's lower half must be screwed without a boss in the battery's path
frame.purpose: low cap screw anchors beside the battery column, clear of the battery and DFR1202 paths
frame.simpler: a short boss hanging off the back face would be a 5 mm overhang in the front-down print pose; rev B1 low bosses behind the pack (+-9, -38.9) blocked the battery's floor push
frame.validation: insertion sweep; access_check on fix y+16.1 z-36.5 and the cap screws; wall check
frame.change_when: a wing is needed for another part or the fixing screw moves

frame.what: M2 pilot 1.95, 0.4 mouth chamfers: through the high bosses, 10 mm blind in the low columns (print_fit pilot depth 9.3)
problems: the cap screws need thread engagement
frame.purpose: self-tapping pilot for the M2 cap screws
frame.simpler: inserts are not in this design's fit practice for M2 in PLA

frame.what: four M2 clearance holes 2.5 through the front wall at the pack post positions
problems: the backpack must fix to the OpenRB pack posts
frame.purpose: pass the four M2 x 6 into the posts

frame.what: 3.5 mm slot in the left wing's step floor, y 22.6..26.1, open to the back to x -60
problems: plug 3 and plug 4 leads must leave the box without threading a connector through a hole
frame.simpler: a closed hole needs the plug threaded through
frame.validation: bought parts clear of the slot

frame.what: front-wall cut around the shell rear lips' projection, grown 0.5
problems: the shell lips reach behind x -45 where the front wall sits
frame.simpler: today's front plate shape (taken from the shells, 0.5 gap)

frame.what: front-wall cut around the wing plate cheeks' (y, z) footprint, grown 0.5, through x -47.5..-44
problems: in flight the backpack sits 6.9 mm back on the wing plate, whose cheeks reach 1.55 mm into the frame's front wall
frame.purpose: no overlap with the flight pack's wing plate
frame.simpler: today's frame front shape (it has the same opening; the concept checked only boxes)

cap.what: back plate x -75.55..-73.85 over both tiers with the lower tier's chamfer
problems: the box must close over the pack, the DFR1202 and the leads
the switch needs a panel to snap into
cap.simpler: an open back leaves the pack exposed

cap.what: three ribs y -19..-17, -6..-4 (to the pack top + 3) and 6..8 (to the pack top), from z -34, through the foam to x -70.3
problems: the pack must not move back
cap.purpose: rear stop of the pack through its foam pad
cap.simpler: foam alone lets the pack move on a fall; the 6..8 rib stops at the pack top under the switch wings

cap.what: tabs on the -19..-17 and -6..-4 ribs over the pack top to x -66
problems: the pack must not lift on a fall (rear side)
cap.purpose: rear top stops clear of the lead exit and of the switch's snap wings (y >= -2.45)

cap.what: four M2 clearance holes 2.5 at the boss positions, 0.4 mouth chamfers
problems: the cap screws pass the cap

cap.what: 27.5 (y) x 12.3 (z) cutout through the cap at (y 13.8, z 35.6), the Swann 39 in it rocker facing back
problems: the robot's on/off switch moves in from today's backpack
rev B's lower tier is the battery column, so the switch cannot sit flush in a floor as today
cap.purpose: the robot's one power switch, reachable from behind, above the flight harness
cap.simpler: floor or side wall: the switch needs 30 mm of flange length and 33.6 mm of depth, which only the cap with the length across y offers; a lower spot on the cap puts the rocker in the flight harness (z 4..28); recessing it needs 8 mm of depth the box lacks
cap.validation: switch envelope overlap 0 with frame, cap and parts; flight overlap 0 with the switch included; wings 0.3 inside the left wall
cap.change_when: the switch is replaced or the flight harness moves

cap.what: two 1.3 mm pads inside the cap at the cutout's ends (y -2.55..0.05 and 27.55..30.15, z 29.85..41.35)
problems: the switch's snap wings were set for today's 3.0 mm floor panel; the cap is 1.7
cap.purpose: make the panel the wings grip 3.0 mm, as today
cap.simpler: a 3 mm cap everywhere adds about 8 g; a 1.7 panel lets the switch rattle 1.3 mm
cap.validation: frame-cap overlap 0 (pads 0.2 from the left wall, 0.25 under the roof); wall check

cap.what: open-top notch 12 (y -25.5..-13.5) x 9 (z 34..43) through the cap
problems: the pack charges through its white 3-pin balance plug on the B3 without opening the backpack
cap.purpose: the balance lead leaves the box here and the plug rests in it, outside, ready for the B3
cap.simpler: a closed hole would need the plug threaded through before the cap goes on; open-top lets the lead drop in after
cap.validation: XH-3P (9.9 x 5.75) passes; 1.75 mm of cap to the high-right screw hole; notch z >= 34 above the flight harness
cap.change_when: the pack's balance lead or the charger changes

removed.rev-B1 low cap bosses (+-9, -38.9), thei: 3.5 mm bosses behind the pack clamped the pad tabs with M2 x 6; with the pads in they and the tabs blocked the battery's floor push (steps_audit bv2-battery, 2026-11-20). Replaced by F11-low-columns in the wings and F8-cap-pad-pins; the pads now go in after the battery.
removed.F4-pololu-ribs: rear rib and ledge for the Pololu 2813: the Pololu power switch is not built (rev M, P-MIN).
removed.F6-xiao-ledge: ledge under the XIAO SAMD21: no XIAO cutoff (rev M, P-MIN).
removed.F6-usb-window: cap window at the XIAO USB-C: no XIAO (rev M).
removed.F7-button-hole: 16.3 mm hole for the PV6 LED button: the robot keeps its Swann 39 rocker (rev M); F13 takes its place in the cap's upper left.
removed.F8-pad-pockets: floor pockets for the Keystone 615 contact pads: no dock charging now (deferred with BatteryDock-B1); the floor goes 2.1 -> 1.4.
removed.F8-cap-pad-pins: cap pins locating the pad tabs: no pads (rev M).
